title: A New Path to Homeownership at Ruby-Mac Place

body_markdown:
We’re out at the Oregon Convention Center attending the Housing Oregon Conference today and tomorrow (September 28-29) and connecting with our design partner, **Nick Mira** from **Propel Studio Architecture** , whose expertise on one of our current projects in Portland, Oregon showcases how sustainability, affordable homeownership and community wealth-building can all come together.


**Ruby-Mac Place** is an ambitious affordable homeownership community led by **Self Enhancement, Inc. (SEI)** in Portland. We’re incredibly proud to be part of the pre-development and design team for this project.


SEI is doing something especially meaningful. They’re creating 49 affordable homes for purchase - not rent - designed to help families build equity and generational wealth in a time where housing is less attainable than ever.


It’s also a challenging 6.5-acre site, with significant wetland and soil conditions that the team has had to design around rather than simply build over. The result will be a mix of cottages, duplexes, townhomes and single-family homes - all designed to achieve **Net Zero Energy** , with solar helping offset the homes’ annual energy consumption.


A big shout-out to the **Portland Clean Energy Community Benefits Fund (PCEF)** for investing in the renewable-energy side of affordable housing and helping make projects like this possible.
